pr_md.text:
What I found: Keep the documented backend capabilities and repair their enforcement (Proceed). The original 20-test suite passed despite missing ownership, lifecycle, money, pagination, and filesystem cases.

Why it matters: Customers could read other customersâ€™ orders; an admin download could escape the export directory. Orders could be cancelled after shipping, totals could drift from exact cents, and declined charges could mark orders paid.

Do this first:
1. Review `test/audit.test.js` alongside the changed services and report route, then run `npm test`.

What I did not check: Production deployment, load/DoS behavior, external payment providers, concurrent filesystem replacement, symlink behavior on target hosts, timing measurements, or a Node-version/OS matrix. Reproduce those in their target environment; no deployment, provider sandbox, benchmark, or matrix command is configured in this repository.

## Changes

- Enforce owner/admin access on individual order reads; keep foreign resources hidden with 404.
- Remove shipped-to-cancelled transition; delivered orders remain terminal.
- Calculate totals in integer cents; reject unsafe quantities, overflowing totals, and totals whose currency-number representation changes their cent value. Compare payments against the canonical order total.
- Refuse uncaptured or malformed provider results before storing a payment or changing order status. Attribute payments to the order owner, including admin-created payments.
- Count partial final pages with `ceil`; parse whole safe positive pagination values rather than accepting numeric prefixes.
- Compare token signatures with length-checked `crypto.timingSafeEqual`.
- Restrict report downloads to generated filenames and real paths inside the report directory. Anchor `/reports/` in `.gitignore`: the previous rule also hid the required `src/reports/routes.js`, which is now included as source.
- Remove the unused cookie parser and redundant line-total/payment-total helpers. Retain provider registration and injection: they are reachable extension points, not proven dead code.

## Evidence

All commands ran locally against uncommitted changes based on `2e01b2ba6f3bee310db666577d07e951eb9918b9`.

| Command/check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm test` before changes | Exit 0; 20 passed, 0 failed |
| `npm test` after changes | Exit 0; 28 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped |
| Independent reviewer: `npm test` | Exit 0; 28 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped |
| Independent boundary assertions | The formerly accepted `0.01 * 9007199254740893` total now throws; ordinary fractional totals remain exact |
| `git diff --check` | Exit 0 |
| Local CommonJS import graph scan | 17 production files, 26 local imports, maximum 3 hops, no cycles |
| New audit tests against original tracked source in a temporary copy | `node --test test/audit.test.js`: exit 1, 7 failed and 1 passed, demonstrating regression sensitivity. Current report source retained because HEAD did not contain it; this countercheck does not validate the original traversal defect. |

The eight new tests exercise authorization, terminal states, pagination boundaries, cent arithmetic/representation, unsafe input, encoded traversal/arbitrary file reads, declined providers, and admin payment ownership. Existing tests remain unchanged.

Independent review found one additional money representation defect, which was fixed and reverified. No other material defect was identified by that review. This is bounded evidence, not proof that the backend has no remaining defects.
